queue.title: Miyamoto Musashi vs Sasaki Kojiro: The Real Duel
The Honnoji Incident: Oda Nobunaga's Betrayal
queue.notes: Akechi Mitsuhide surrounds Honno-ji temple with 10,000 soldiers. June 21, 1582. Teased in ep001 outro.

queue.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu: How a Hostage Became a Shogun
queue.notes: Held hostage as a child, became Japan's ultimate unifier. The ultimate long game.

queue.title: The Battle of Sekigahara: One Day That Decided Japan
queue.notes: October 21, 1600. 160,000 troops. The decisive battle that created 250 years of Tokugawa rule.

queue.title: Tomoe Gozen: Japan's Greatest Female Warrior
queue.notes: Rare female samurai. Historical debates about her fate. Strong hook potential.

queue.title: The 47 Ronin: Japan's Most Famous Act of Loyalty
queue.notes: 47 masterless samurai avenge their lord 2 years after his forced seppuku. 1703.

queue.title: Oda Nobunaga: The Demon King Who Almost United Japan
queue.notes: The most radical warlord. Destroyed Buddhist monasteries, embraced firearms, upended feudal order.

queue.title: The Ninja: Separating Myth from History
queue.notes: What ninja actually were vs. pop culture myth. Iga and Koga clans. Historical espionage.

queue.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi: From Sandal-Bearer to Ruler of Japan
queue.notes: Born a peasant, became supreme ruler. The most dramatic rise in Japanese history.

queue.title: The Siege of Osaka: The Fall of the Toyotomi
queue.notes: 1614-1615. Tokugawa eliminates the last Toyotomi heir. End of the Sengoku era.

queue.title: The Way of the Samurai: Bushido's True Origins
queue.notes: Bushido as a concept was mostly invented in the Edo period — not medieval. Interesting revisionism angle.

queue.title: Takeda Shingen vs Uesugi Kenshin: The Eternal Rivals
queue.notes: Five battles of Kawanakajima. Famous rivals with a grudging respect. Rich drama.

queue.title: The Battle of Nagashino: The Day Firearms Changed Japan
queue.notes: 1575. Nobunaga's volley fire destroys Takeda cavalry. Technological turning point.

queue.title: Seppuku: The Truth Behind Japan's Ritual Suicide
queue.notes: History, ritual, meaning. Why it existed and what it meant culturally. Sensitive but compelling.

queue.title: Date Masamune: The One-Eyed Dragon of the North
queue.notes: Aggressive warlord of Sendai domain. Lost one eye to smallpox. Ambitious but born too late.

queue.title: The Shimabara Rebellion: Japan's Last Samurai Battle
queue.notes: 1637-1638. Christian peasants vs. the shogunate. 37,000 defenders vs. 120,000 shogunate troops.

queue.title: Maeda Toshiie: The Spear Master Who Challenged Nobunaga
queue.notes: One of Nobunaga's top generals. Famous spear fighter. Complicated loyalty.

queue.title: The Black Ships: When Commodore Perry Broke Japan Open
queue.notes: 1853. Four steam warships force Japan to end 250 years of isolation. Triggers samurai era's end.

queue.title: The Last Samurai: Saigo Takamori and the Satsuma Rebellion
queue.notes: 1877. Final armed samurai uprising. The real story behind the Tom Cruise movie.

queue.title: Women of the Warring States: The Wives Behind the Warlords
queue.notes: Oichi, Nene, Lady Tsukiyama. Political marriages, tragedy, survival. Female perspective on Sengoku.

queue.title: The Book of Five Rings: Musashi's Philosophy Explained
queue.notes: Deep dive into Go Rin No Sho — strategy, void, water, fire. Companion to ep001.

queue.title: Uesugi Kenshin: The Buddhist Warlord Who Never Lost
queue.notes: Famous for personal religious discipline. Claimed to fight for justice, not conquest. Complex character.

queue.title: The Siege of Hara Castle: 37,000 vs. 120,000
queue.notes: Final act of Shimabara Rebellion. Siegecraft, desperation, and massacre. Visual/dramatic potential.

queue.title: Sanada Yukimura: Japan's Greatest Loser
queue.notes: Brilliant tactician on the losing side. Died at Osaka, age ~49. Revered despite defeat. Great hook.

queue.title: The Ronin: Life Without a Master in Feudal Japan
queue.notes: Social phenomenon of masterless samurai. Poverty, stigma, and survival. Contextual explainer.

queue.title: Katana: The Science and Soul of Japan's Sacred Sword
queue.notes: Metallurgy, folding technique, tamahagane steel. Separating myth from craft.

queue.title: The Mongol Invasions: When Japan Was Nearly Conquered
queue.notes: 1274 and 1281. Kublai Khan's massive fleets. The kamikaze (divine winds) that saved Japan.

queue.title: Hattori Hanzo: The Real Ninja Behind the Legend
queue.notes: The historical Hattori Hanzo was Tokugawa Ieyasu's head of secret service. Very different from fiction.

queue.title: Yoshitsune: The Tragic Hero of the Genpei War
queue.notes: 12th century. Military genius betrayed by his own brother Yoritomo. Iconic tragic arc.

queue.title: The Rise of the Shogunate: How Warriors Took Power from the Emperor
queue.notes: How Minamoto no Yoritomo created the first shogunate in 1192. Structural explainer. Good early episode.
